newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia sugar expansion not guaranteed - growers.
newsitem.headline: Australia sugar expansion not guaranteed - growers.

text.p: Recent impressive expansion and productivity performances by the Australian sugar industry do not guarantee a similar track record in the future, grower organisation Canegrowers said in a statement on Monday.
A powerful lineup of world sugar experts would inform cane growers of this at a major sugar conference in Brisbane, beginning on Tuesday, Canegrowers said.

The 450 delegates attending the Australian Sugar Convention would be told that loss of Australia's sugar tariff, impending changes to sugar industry legislation and major restructuring of the world sugar market would place more pressure on Australian
cane growers and sugar millers to be more efficient and productive, it said.

The convention, held every three years, is due to open with the annual general meeting of Canegrowers, the peak body representing the canegrowing industry. Queensland premier Rob Borbidge will address the meeting on Tuesday.

Canegrowers general manager Ian Ballantyne said growers, gearing up for another big harvest, would be eager to hear Borbidge define the state government's vision of the future operating environment for the sugar industry.
Ballantyne and Canegrowers chairman Harry Bonanno will report on the recent performance of the growers' organisation and outline the growers position on key industry issues.
International sugar marketing expert John Barneby, managing director, Czarnikow Ltd, London, is to brief brief growers on changing market trends and price prospects.

Nearly 450 registrations have been received from Australia, Britain, the U.S., Canada, France, Denmark, Mauritius, Swaziland, South Africa, Fiji, Singapore, Hong Kong, Papua New Guinea, Philippines, Thailand, India and Guyana.
The conference is to be addressed also by Deputy Prime Minister Tim Fischer.
